articles.summary: There are eight Characters in Final Fantasy Resonance, each filling a specific role such as Sentinel, Breaker, Commando, and more. This guide details all eight
articles.body:
There are eight Characters in Final Fantasy Resonance, each filling a specific role such as Sentinel, Breaker, Commando, and more. This guide details all eight FInal Fantasy Resonance playable characters, with information on when you recruit them and their specialty.

Rain is a knight of the Kingdom of Grandshelt and the main protagonist of Final Fantasy Resonance. He is mainly a physical attacker, though his highest attributes are his health and defense making him the beefiest character through the whole game.

Rain's skills include Fire skills and magic, as well as defensive abilities like Protect and Provoke.

Lasswell is Rain's adopted brother and fellow knight of Grandshelt. He is mainly a physical attacker, but also has one of the highest Speed stat in the game. His physical attack is higher even than Rain's by default.

Lasswell's skills include Ice skills and magic, Haste, and multiple buffs he can place on himself to raise his damage and speed potential even higher.

Fina is a mysterious girl who comes to Rain and Lasswell's assistance, then joins their party early in the story. She is mainly a healer, with the highest Sanctity stat in the game.

Fina's skills include a wide variety of white magic, as well as Light magic. She also has a number of unique buffs, like Cheer and Arcane Guard, making her an incredible support throughout the entire game.

Fina is also one of two characters who can Summon Espers, giving her a unique edge in battle.

Lid is a plucky Airship engineer who joins the party early in the game. Her highest attribute is Stamina, but really she is a jack-of-all-trades type with solid stats in everything. Use her to fill any role you need.

Lid's skills include Earth skills and magic, as well as Mechabo attacks. She does not learn many skills by leveling up. Instead, her kit is expanded via a series of sub quests where you upgrade her Mechabo.

Nichol is a strategist who joins the party early in the game. His highest attribute is Magic, but he also boasts one of the highest Speed stats in the game. He has a wide variety of buffs that make him a great support, but in the late game he also becomes the best and most versatile healer in the game as well.

Nichol's skills include Water skills and magic. He has a unique set of buffs known as Formations which raise various stats of the whole party. His other special skill, Tactic: Fluid Warfare, lets him take two turns in a row.

Jake is the leader of a rebel army who leaves his country to join the party. His highest attribute is Strength, and he is actually the strongest physical attacker in the game though some of his other stats are lacking.

Jake's skills revolve around his unique Coin Toss skill and Luck mechanic, which determines which skills he can use and the strength of those skills. He also has Wind magic, and Bravery right in his default kit.

Sakura is a centuries old wizard who joins the party later in the game. She has the highest magic attack stat of anyone, making her the best spellcaster by default.

Sakura's skill include a variety of powerful magic and buffs. She has Lightning, Light, and Dark magic, as well as Flare and Meteor. She has a unique Dispel in Magicide, and her buffs, like Concentrate, further increase her magic attack.

Archwitch Fina is another ancient warrior, and the alter ego of Fina. Her highest attribute is Magic, but she is a hybrid attacker with solid physical attacking potential as well. Her main role is inflicting debuffs on enemies.

Archwitch Fina's skills include Dark skills and magics, as well as Meteor and Ultima. She has a number of debuffs, including the powerful Queenly Whip which reduces enemy attack stats. She can further increase her Dark damage with her Paradise Lost skill, at the cost of reducing other damage types.

Archwitch Fina is also one of two characters who can Summon Espers , giving her a unique edge in battle.

articles.body:
MRP, or Mastery Rank Points , are a secondary form of Experience that serves to level up your Visions in Final Fantasy Resonance. All enemies award a small amount of MRP, which might leave you wondering how to farm MRP.

This IGN guide will detail the best enemies and methods for MRP farming in Final Fantasy Resonance.

Cactuars are a classic Final Fantasy enemy known for being elusive and rewarding high amount of Experience. In Final Fantasy Resonance, there are two types of Cactuar: the regular green ones, and Metal ones. The green Cactuars award MRP, while the Metal ones award EXP .

There are three ways to defeat Cactuars:

Ice and Water attacks. Cactuars are weak to Ice and Water and hitting them with these attacks gives a better chance of stagger. Multi-hit moves, like Blizzara or Nichol's Aqua Blast, give even better odds of staggering and killing.

Noctis's Barrage skill . The overall best attack for farming Cactuars is Barrage, which can be learned by leveling up the Noctis Vision. This move is guaranteed to hit, and also hits 4 times. Even better, you get Noctis relatively early in the game.

Amelia's Aim skill . Finally we have Amelia's Aim skill, a buff that guarantees all attacks will hit. This is technically the best way to hit Cactuars, but you get Amelia very late in the game so Noctis will prove more universally usable.

There are three types of green Cactuar in Resonance:

Minituar , found in north Grandshelt desert east of the Esper sealing stone.

Cactuar , found in southern Zoldaad, near Pyroviper Cave

Gigantuar can be found in central Gronoa in Chapter 6. However, you can actually encounter the Gigantuar a little early by landing on this small piece of land on the back side of Gronoa, allowing you to find Gigantuar as soon as you get the Airship.

Gigantuar can also be encountered on the small island outside the exit of Dragon's Maw. This island cannot be reached via Airship, and you will need to complete Dragon's Maw to get there.

Citrine Pots, previously known as Magic Pots, are the other way to quickly get MRP, though their uses are more limited than Cactuars. You will see these Golden Pots in various dungeons throughout the game. Examine them to trigger a battle.

In the battle, the Citrine Pot will demand an item, usually a type of Ether. Use the requested item on the Citrine Pot to "win" the battle, and get a huge amount of MRP.

Because there is no actual combat make sure you are switching to Expert difficulty before encountering them! It is free MRP . If you don't have the requested item you can always come back later, though remember each Citrine Pot is single use.

Up Next: Cactuar Locations (How to Beat Cactuar)

articles.body:
An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Sega’s beloved mascot character, Sonic the Hedgehog .

The heartbreaking story comes from West Yorkshire in the UK, where a male hedgehog was found with extensive chemical burns after being spray-painted blue by supposed vandals. The animal was discovered outside the Wakefield police station and subsequently brought to Castleford Hedgehog Rescue on Tuesday, October 27, for treatment.

Unfortunately, the poor critter didn’t make it. Local reports state that the spray paint literally burned through “several layers” of the hedgehog’s skin, to the point where it melted its spines, causing extreme pain.

29-year-old Beth Campbell, who operates the hedgehog rescue, says she tried everything in her power to help — but the pain was so severe that the defenseless animal literally “screamed himself to death.”

"I don't know how anyone could be so cruel to an animal. It is disgusting,” she told YorkshireLive. "I haven't seen anything as bad or as sad as this in a long time. …I'm glad he was brought in, as it meant at least we could ease his suffering and make him feel comfortable."

Campbell says the spray paint gave the hedgehog significant chemical burns that, in turn, triggered an infection on its now-exposed skin. This, along with potential poisoning from the chemicals in the spray paint, is what ultimately caused its death.

She also revealed that the hedgehog was suffering from a condition known as flystrike, which occurs when flies lay their eggs in animals’ open wounds or soft tissue, resulting in maggots that feast on their flesh. Spray paint aside, Campbell said that the critter would have likely undergone a "slow and ultimately and extremely painful death" in the wild.

On Facebook , the hedgehog rescued posted a heartwrenching tribute to the deceased hedgehog: “As a result of cruelty our poor boy has passed away. This has deeply affected our volunteers and myself as he laid screaming in pain, he was given the full amount of pain relief he could have," the group wrote.

“Rest peacefully little man, the way you were treated was horrific, we tried everything we possibly could to save you, but you were too precious for this cruel world. Pain free, running free across the rainbow bridge.”

Campbell said she plans to report the incident to police, but is unsure if any action will be taken, given the location where the animal was found. Thus far, no arrests have been made, and local police have not released a statement regarding the matter.

Hedgehogs are listed as a nearly threatened species globally and are classified as vulnerable for extinction within the UK. Populations of the animal have dropped between 30-75% since 2000, with expanding human activity impacting their ability to find food, shelter, and otherwise survive.

articles.title: MTG Darkhold Destiny 4 Commander Deck Bundles: Do They Look Good or Not?
articles.summary: Are MTG Darkhold Destiny's Commander bundles worth $299.96 or $639.96? Here's what's included and whether the four decks look promising enough.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering’s latest Marvel crossover is still nearly six months away, but Amazon preorders are already up for bundles containing four Darkhold Destiny Commander decks, though one is definitely more hefty in ptice than the other.

Whilst the standard four-deck bundle is currently selling for $299.96 on Amazon , the Collector’s Edition is going for $639.96 — both sold directly by the retailer, and launching on April 9, 2027.

Depending on which one you’re eyeing up, this works out to $74.99 or $159.99 each respectively. Understandably, that’s quite a high entry price and knock on potential trading card budgets, so you need to know exactly what you’re getting for your money, and whether that initial cost seems worthwhile, based on first impressions.

Collector’s Edition - Commander Deck Bundle

What comes in the Darkhold Destiny Commander Bundles?

No matter which price you pay, either Darkhold Destiny Commander bundle comes with the following decks: Strange Academy, Gods of Asgard, Midnight Sons, and Lords of Hel.

Each deck has 100 cards and is completely ready-to-play, containing 30 new-to-Magic Commander cards; that’s along with ten double-sided tokens, a deck box, and a strategy guide.

The difference between the two bundles is that the standard version comes with two Traditional Foil legendary creatures per deck; the Collector’s Editions, meanwhile, swap in Surge Foil treatments across all 100 cards.

Do these Commander decks actually look good?

Amongst the many preorders up for Darkhold Destiny in general, the Commander Decks definitely look at least interesting on paper.

For instance, with Strange Academy, Doctor Strange leads a white-blue-black blink deck that’s built around sending creatures out of play and bringing them back to make repeated use of their enter-the-battlefield effects, as pointed out by Wargamer . Since it’s quite a tried-and-tested strategy, there could be plenty of mileage with this deck, though it depends what the new cards will actually do effects-wise.

Meanwhile, Lords of Hel has Hela commanding a red-black token sacrifice deck; that’s another promising combo, but that depends on the payoff you get for sacrificing those creatures. In contrast, Thor’s red-green-white Gods of Asgard focuses on equipment and creatures with power four or more, whilst Blade’s white-black Midnight Sons revolves around Vampires, building life, and spending it to trigger abilities.

Considering the price, it is at least a relief to see that these are four Marvel-themed decks with more variety than doing the same thing. Plus, with the expansion itself, as we learned when it was announced , Darkhold Destiny is set to be the first Universes Beyond set building around an original story shared between Marvel and Wizards of the Coast.

On the other hand, until we see the full decklists, we can’t at least 100% determine whether all decks will be objectively good in the game’s meta when Darkhold Destiny comes out. That said, if you loved the original Marvel Super Heroes expansion and are excited to see more, it should be at least safe to pre-order the standard $299.96 bundle — and wait until further down the line to decide on the Collector’s Editions.

articles.title: Crimson Desert: Charting the Unknown Review So Far
articles.summary: After six hours with this beefy DLC, it seems to add even more to Crimson Desert’s buffet-style approach while doing little to improve existing systems.
articles.body:
Crimson Desert’s biggest strength is in the sheer volume of stuff it throws at you, allowing you to spend hundreds or even a thousand-plus hours doing everything from hunting animals with a bow to developing a gambling addiction at the tavern. So it’s not very surprising that Crimson Desert’s first paid DLC, called Charting the Unknown, prioritizes adding more on top of its already staggeringly large repertoire. So far, the interesting new activities that mostly focus on oceanic adventures are exactly as compelling as you’d hope, with ship-to-ship combat, underwater exploration, and romance options being among the list of new worthwhile features. On the other hand, existing activities that have added content, like the extra story missions, have mostly been uninspired retreads that don’t do anything to improve upon their established shortcomings. When Crimson Desert came out, I said that its content was a mile long and an inch deep, and for better or worse this DLC seems to say, “Here’s another half-mile.”

The most disappointing part of the DLC so far has been the additional story missions, which are only accessible once you’ve completed the base game’s already dense main story (a feat which only 10% of Steam players have done, judging by the achievements system). At least the handful of missions I’ve completed at this point have mostly served as an expanded epilogue of sorts, with Kliff fighting more difficult versions of old bosses from the existing story, and Damiane and Oongka fleshing out their less substantial stories as well.

Crimson Desert Enhanced: Charting the Unknown Screenshots

I’m not far enough to know if any of these quests eventually become more interesting, but most of their objectives have been an oddly bland retracing of your steps, like going back to spend time with a familiar character and share a moment fishing together or arm wrestle someone to gather information as an apparent callback to an identical moment in the original story. I did get to a new stretch of the map just before getting distracted by the separate seafaring content, so hopefully this part of the DLC will pick up the pace, but so far it’s been about as unimpressive as I expected given the low bar for storytelling in Crimson Desert.

Much like the base content though, most of the effort seems to have been put into things that aren’t related to the story. Although most of my time has been spent dipping my toes into the water-based ship-crafting feature that’s the focus of this expansion, it feels like I’ve only seen the tip of the iceberg, with new resources to obtain, crewmates to hire, and even more activities to learn like harpooning fish and ship-to-ship combat before you can really begin your voyages properly.

It's going to take more time to fully engage with these new activities and judge whether or not they have the sea legs to keep me entertained for longer than a few hours, but at least right now I’m just impressed (yet again) by the fact that these systems exist in this adventure that’s already so damn packed with things to do. Gliding underwater on the back of a sea turtle and captaining your own pirate crew truly just feel completely bizarre in the context of Crimson Desert, and so far that’s been compelling enough to keep me moving forward even if some of the other added content isn’t great.

There’s still a ton I have to investigate, like additional base building and property management features, a challenging combat arena-style gauntlet, and my personal favorite – social links and romance mechanics for NPCs, which I’m very excited to check out once I’ve gotten my bearings (I’m just not ready to settle down yet, okay?!).

For all the stuff that’s been added, one thing that is the same since the last time I played is the number of bugs I’ve encountered in my brief time with the Charting the Unknown DLC. I’ve already had two hard crashes, one character wig out on me while I was trying to arm wrestle him (he was hilariously standing behind me during the match, arm bent unnaturally), and quite a few blurry or flickering textures that are impossible for me to not focus on during cutscenes. I’m still too early to tell if this is going to be a consistent issue, but in my time so far it’s been quite rocky from a technical perspective considering how much wonkiness I’ve encountered per hour played.

As expected with Crimson Desert, it’s going to take quite a bit of time to see and do enough to reach a definitive conclusion on Charting the Unknown, and I’m hopeful that the engaging and unexpected content that’s been added will be able to make up for some of the activities that feel like empty calories.

articles.title: VRChat Devs Spark Outrage After Refusing to Include AI Label Despite 95% of Fans Asking for It
articles.summary: The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey.
articles.body:
The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey.

VRChat is a virtual hub where folks can gather to chat, make their own avatars, and create and play games together. It’s a fairly popular social platform that, perhaps unsurprisingly, is a hotbed for viral moments and hilarious content.

Also unsurprisingly, there’s been a sharp increase in AI-generated content in VRChat, to the point where fans are begging for some sort of distinction as to what has and hasn’t been made by humans.

Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Dual Destinies VR Screenshots

In fact, the folks behind VRChat recently published a survey asking users for their feedback on the state of the platform. In that survey, “95% of survey respondents want some kind of label for AI usage,” as told in an official blog published on October 28.

Despite this overwhelming majority, the powers that be have decided against moving forward with an AI label, arguing that there’s simply too much disagreement among users as to what, exactly, should be done to delineate such content.

“We’re not adding an ‘AI-generated’ label or AI filters,” the devs said in the blog post. “While we think some creators would honestly label their content, we think others would try to pass off generative or assisted work as completely authored by hand. Likewise, we could see this creating ‘sleuthing’ behavior, where folks would attempt to sniff out ‘AI’ content or might harass other creators, even if they are genuinely not using any AI tools in their workflow. We think this potentially creates negative behavior spirals we don’t want to encourage.”

The statement continued, revealing that respondents gave “3,141 different combinations of labeling,”and that “no single combination was given by more than 10% of respondents.”

Essentially, the team at VRChat feels they need to “understand this a layer deeper before making any kneejerk decisions” — but their explanation hasn’t been well-received by fans.

On social media, dedicated VRChat users are speaking out against this decision, with one writing on X/Twitter, “Then what was the point of the survey if they’re not going to f**king use it to influence decisions?”

“95% of YOUR players said NO to AI content. That isn't a debatable margin,” another argued .

“The point of having a filter is because we do NOT want to see that content. They are FILTERS for a reason, bruh,” another exasperated user wrote .

Thus far, VRChat has made no official response to this outrage and is continuing to move forward with planned events, leaving users beside themselves as they work to make their voices heard by the platform.

articles.title: Everything Coming to HBO Max in November
articles.body:
Warner Bros. has revealed a hefty lineup of new additions coming to HBO Max in November. The streaming service is diving right into the holiday vibes on November 1, rolling out a spread of classic Christmas movies in addition to its annual "Yule Log" ambient videos. In the thick of the festivities, HBO Max will also be picking up solid non-festive movie marathons and recent A24 releases.

While there’s no big DC premieres this month (unless you count Clayface in theaters, which will eventually come to HBO Max), there are still some treats for the superhero-inclined. And, as always, subscribers will get access to a complicated splattering of live sports.

Highlights Coming to HBO Max in November

Check out our top picks coming to HBO Max in November or jump ahead to the full release schedule by day .

Next Big HBO Original: The Gilded Age Season 4

First up, what’s filling the classic HBO Sunday slot? The Pet Cemetery Murders: A Ghost Story miniseries wrapped up over the course of October, and Season 4 of The Gilded Age will take its place starting November 1.

From the creator of Downtown Abbey, The Gilded Age is a similar period-accurate drama that, as the title suggests, takes place in late-19th century New York. The new season will release one episode every Sunday through mid-December, leading up to the premiere of HBO’s new Harry Potter series .

HBO Max continues to be the streaming home for A24 releases, and the big one coming to the service in November is Tony. Matthew Johnson’s Anthony Bourdain biopic loosely adapts the first couple of chapters of Kitchen Confidential, painting a very New England picture of how the writer-chef-TV personality first fell in love with the food industry.

Tony is one of IGN’s best-reviewed movies of 2026 so far, with critic Siddhant Adhlaka deeming it “one of the finest and thorniest coming-of-age films in recent years” in his full review .

For Your Next Movie Marathon: Planet of the Apes

While the original 1968 Planet of the Apes movie continues to be near-impossible to find on streaming, HBO Max will be picking up four of the newer Apes movies on November 2. The new quartet, which kicked off with Rise of the Apes in 2011, forms its own timeline which trades the original movie’s nuclear apocalypse for a human-made virus.

We were particularly big fans of the most recent release, Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes, with critic Eric Goldman arguing it “proves there's still a lot of life in these primates.” Disney seems to feel the same way, given they’ve greenlit yet another reboot of the franchise.

While there aren't any new DC Studios releases coming to streaming next month, a few older superhero movies will be available to HBO Max subscribers for the first time. If you haven’t witnessed the infamous Madame Web , that’s one option. But if you’re looking for a movie with some actual action (sorry, Madame Web fans), HBO Max will also be picking up the first Wolverine movie.

Whether you enjoyed or felt let down by Insomniac’s recent take on the clawed hero, the HBO Max addition is a solid opportunity to revisit what we considered “the Wolverine movie we've always wanted” in our 9/10 review .

It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise, but HBO Max subscribers should keep an eye out for a massive influx of classic Christmas and holiday movies. Elf, A Christmas Carol, Christmas With the Kranks, and National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation are just a few of the many classics that are making their way to HBO Max this year. Expect to see holiday-themed sections throughout the streaming service’s app, roping together existing shows and movies with November’s new additions.

articles.title: Liam Neeson Continues His Late-In-Life Action Star Antics With The Mongoose, a Film That’s Heavy on Car Chases and Light on Plot
articles.summary: Review: Liam Neeson continues his late-in-life action star antics with The Mongoose, a film that’s heavy on car chases and light on plot.
articles.body:
There’s a scene in the 1971 sci-fi cult classic The Omega Man where Charlton Heston’s helicopter is crash-landing, and just before the moment of impact it flies into an embankment just below the camera’s POV… where the craft’s explosion happens safely off-screen. It was a cheapo move in 1971 – they clearly didn’t really blow up the helicopter – and it’s a cheapo move in 2026, too, when Liam Neeson’s The Mongoose – now, somehow, playing at a multiplex near you! – pulls a similar stunt.

Sure, in The Mongoose the helicopter doesn’t even blow up off-camera, but that’s not the point (the crash-landing winds up being played for a laugh instead). What I’m talking about here is the threadbare sense that such a moment evokes for the viewer, the “a third of the budget of this movie must’ve gone to Liam Neeson” feeling that permeates the not-quite high-octane, not-quite thrilling picture.

And yet, there’s a likability factor wafting around this story, thanks largely to Neeson’s disarming “yeah, I am taking a third of this film’s budget, and I’m gonna have fun doing it” affectation as he drives a stolen hotrod – do we still call them hotrods? – across various states while on the run from the police due to a crime he did not commit. Along for the ride, so to speak, are Ving Rhames, Marisa Tomei, and Michael Chiklis, all cashing in less than a third of the budget, presumably, but hitting their marks efficiently enough to get this thing over the finish line in a “Maybe just catch it on Prime Video eventually” kind of way.

The Mongoose tells its story through a mix of the chase Neeson’s Ryan “Fang” Flanagan is involved in and flashbacks to the former Special Forces soldier’s time in Afghanistan, specifically when he and his comrades (Rhames’ Tanker, Marcus Thomas’ Munch, and Ryan Morgan's Wiz) were captured by the enemy. Further flashbacks eventually fill in why Fang is on the run; specifically, his ex-wife Tara’s (Marisa Tomei) fiancé – “Todd something or other,” Fang growls – turns out to be not a nice person, and when Fang attempts to help Tara move out of the guy’s place, violence erupts. Next thing he knows, someone’s dead, and he’s stolen Todd something or other’s fancy, and quite fast, Ford Mustang. Other than that, all he’s got is a bullet in his leg, a vow to never be imprisoned again after his experience in the war, and the Mustang's built-in AI assistant, named Helene. “Is this, like, Siri?” Fang – and maybe Neeson too when he first read the script – asks.

Helene, like many of the other characters (“characters”) in the episodic The Mongoose, serves as a foil for the surprisingly at-ease Fang to toss one-liners at while out-driving the various police who are pursuing him by land and air. Fang is surprisingly chill about this situation, as he clearly has a death wish, having decided that he is not going to allow himself to be taken alive. As the chase drags on, he eventually finds temporary refuge through the help of some other vets, and soon Fang begins to take on a legendary man-against-the-system status, thanks no doubt to his war hero cred, as well as the “live” CNN coverage of the high-speed pursuit, which IRL TV personality Laura Coates awkwardly hosts.

On the side of the law, there’s Maurice Marvel Meredith as Major James Tilton and Chiklis as Major Walter Pope. Suffice to say, one’s the good cop and one’s the bad copy, and never the twain shall meet, but also, never the twain shall have anything interesting or realistic to do or say. Rhames, unfortunately, seems to be struggling to deliver his lines at times, even while his very presence brings a sense of good will to the film. Tomei, meanwhile, is always likable, but most of her scenes are essentially just her on the phone with Neeson’s character, even as she miraculously overcomes some seriously life-changing events over the course of 24 hours or so.

As for the Mongoose of the title, it’s the beach in Mexico where Fang and Tara had their best days together, and as such it’s the ideal that Fang has fixated on – his “retirement” – if he somehow can escape his current, dire situation. But what he also must escape is the guilt of the men he left behind in Afghanistan, and it is this thread that director Mark Vanselow somehow scores with by the time the credits roll, aided no doubt by some keenly picked, and timed, needledrops, and a couple of very cleverly edited shots in the final moments of the film. The Mongoose may be working just one level above a direct-to-video cheapie for a lot of its running time, but it’s still got some heart, too.

articles.title: Best Perks - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN
articles.summary: After you complete your first run in Probably Stolen, a list of perks becomes available to you when you start a new game. There are multiple positive and
articles.body:
After you complete your first run in Probably Stolen , a list of perks becomes available to you when you start a new game. There are multiple positive and negative perks, giving you the opportunity to pick up to four different ones, granted you use the set amount of points you have. Some of these perks stand out as notable options, and are some we highly recommend that you can use when you play. In this guide, we'll be covering the best perks you can get in Probably Stolen.

You can pick up to four perks (unless you get the Colorful Character, and then you can add up to three more). However, you cannot exceed the three-perk-point limit, meaning you do have to accept negative ones, or ones that are worth zero. The negative perk points typically come with a difficulty, making your gameplay harder to some degree.

These are some of the best perks that you can get in Probably Stolen. Some of these perks are negative, but the downsides you get from them are not too bad, depending on your playstyle.

Agoraphobia limits the number of times you can go out. If you go out once, you have to wait two days before you can go out again. This is for any outside activity. As a negative trait, it does give you a plus one to your perk points, which can be an exceptionally good one.

Although the negative does prevent you from visiting any of the outdoor locations, it's not entirely horrible, especially if you plan your trips accordingly. You don't always have to go to these locations, as they are optional. If there are other traits you want to grab for your run, getting this one as a negative choice is a good offset to everything else.

Convict is a negative trait that you start with negative 30 Security reputation, and you receive 25% less reward whenever you turn in anyone from the Wanted List. Starting out on the Security's bad side can be tough, but it's not horrible, especially if you're not planning to go out of your way to be difficult toward them. You'll get one additional perk point for choosing this option.

If you're starting as a Chemist , or someone who will be doing multiple illegal activities, grabbing this one might not be a good idea. But other starting professions might appreciate this, such as any of the more legal ones, or if you're planning on doing illegal activities later in your playthrough. When you're negative with the Security, they might perform more searches at your vendor, so make sure to have a Smuggling container to hide from them.

Diplomatic is a positive perk and gives you 33% more reputation when conducting trades. Because of how beneficial this option is, it costs two perk points, and it's hard to beat it.

Reputation with the various factions can take you a long way through your playthrough. You'll be able to get on a side's good side far faster with this, especially as you make positive trades and barters with them. For anyone who is consistently making products or selling to a specific side, Diplomatic is fantastic.

Hoarder is a neutral perk, where you get zero points for having it. It does not take away anything from you, other than taking up one of your four starting perk slots.

With Hoarder, you start with three different piles of junk that are stuck in your shop's inventory. These are fairly big and limit how many items you can have in your shop. However, you can pick away at these piles as time, such as taking away one piece at a time from the smaller piles if you don't go out at night to earn items. One of the larger ones does require tools to remove, but once these are gone, you'll get the items from them, and you won't have to deal with them anymore. It's a good choice for anyone who's planning to focus on materials and items.

Intimidating is a positive perk that requires you to spend two perk points to have it. With it, any crime you commit gives the Security 33% less evidence.

It'll be harder for the Security to build a case against you if they don't like you on the station. For anyone who's looking to perform illegal activities, such as selling drugs, weapons, or any type of contraband, this is a good way to make it harder for the Security to apprehend you.

Maimed is a negative perk that gives you an additional perk point. With it, you won't be able to visit the Dumping Grounds when the night activities start, preventing you from visiting this location.

For anyone who doesn't plan to head there to gather random materials or loot items that others talk about, it's not a huge loss. The Dumping Grounds can be a mildly beneficial place, but if you're focusing on certain activities at your vendor, going out might not be as good an option if you can stay inside and get another customer the next day. Maimed is a good way to benefit from this choice of never visiting the Dumping Grounds.

Sawyer's Crew is a positive perk that you can get for one perk point. The Underground Exchange group is available to you immediately, and it doesn't cost anything to get the Janitorial service at night, except if your shop is vandalized at a reduced cost.

This is a great all-around perk for any player in Probably Stolen. It cuts down the nightly costs you normally expect to pay, and you keep all of the benefits for it. Plus, if something does happen, like vandalism, it doesn't cost as much.

Short Sleeper is a positive perk that you can get for one perk point. With it, whenever you go out at night, you'll be able to get up early enough that you don't miss out on that one customer you normally lose.

The Short Sleeper perk is a good one for those who plan to reliably use the nighttime activities (not someone who's using the Maimed perk). If you're planning to frequent the Dumping Grounds as often as you can, this is a great option.

The Sycophant is a positive perk that you can get for one perk point. You now start with a 15 plus bonus to the Upper Levels Reputation faction, and you gain 25% more reputation with them whenever it happens. They also have 10% more of a budget.

For anyone who wants to regularly sell to the Upper Level citizens who come through, this is a great way to capitalize on their arrival. You might always be able to predict when they're going to arrive, or what they want, but when they do come through, expect to make a lot of money. Given their frequency, this can be good for anyone crafting items in their shop.

The Vending Machine is a positive perk that you can get for one perk point. You start with the Vending Machine across from your store, and you can sell items there to customers at night.

If you feel that you want to expand the number of customers who can buy from you, adding the legal items to this vending machine is a good way to make sure it gets to them at all times of the day. You do have to maintain it, though, which can be challenging, but it becomes easier as time goes on.

Wild's Favorite is a positive perk that you can get for one perk point. All of Wild's upgrades cost 10% less, and insurance costs 50% less every night.

Wild's upgrades are great to get in the early game, but you don't need them as often as you progress. Still, not having to spend as much money upfront is always good, plus lowering the price of insurance is a great bonus if you don't want to ever lose your items at night. Especially if you're using a vending machine!

Working Pipes is a positive perk that you can get for two perk points. You start out with a water line directly in your shop, and you can get Rustwater from it.

For those who are planning to start off as a Water Merchant, this is a great way to have a reliable supply on hand from the start. You do have to clean and filter this water, which does cost money. But the eventual benefits from this can be fantastic if you capitalize on this early and get customers in when there's a water shortage.

articles.title: Bungie Says 'Don't Buy Marathon as a Donation' as Destiny Players Look to Support Studio's Future
articles.summary: As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny, head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
articles.body:
As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny , head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.

It's a clarification that arrived after Deane posted a community message for Destiny fans yesterday. The message, featured as part of a lengthy Q&A blog post , outlined the unvaulting process for Destiny 2 content that was previously promised last month, but one segment left players confused – and concerned – about the future and extraction shooter Marathon's role in the big picture.

"We're not going to forget the mistakes of the past, but it's time to learn from them and unify as one Bungie community," the section in question said. "For us, the majority of our Bungie team is legacy Destiny, and we will all tell you that nothing can help bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable. As we head into our December and March updates for Marathon, it’s a formative period for all of us here at Bungie that will help determine the shape of our future, so please encourage each other and know that your support gives our team the energy to finish the fight."

It's the "nothing can help us bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable" bit that's got the Destiny community so riled up. With the back-and-forth pulling Destiny 2 in and out of the fire all through the span of a few months, some believed Bungie was trying to tell its audience that picking up a copy of its new sci-fi FPS would help keep it and the studio's future secure. Deane stepped in to confirm this is not the case.

The Bungie developer said his intention was not to rest the Destiny revival on the shoulders of the fans that helped breathe life back into it earlier this year. He chalks it up to a mistranslation, "and that's on me."

"In no way is the Destiny plan contingent upon Marathon," Deane added. "Play what inspires you, whatever it is. Mainly hoping we can accomplish our goals in both lanes with a stronger relationship with our entire community!"

I may have worded this clumsily but this is the true heart of what I was trying to say Truly care about community healing and believe that it will help our studio bridge into the future in the most healthy way possible ❤️ Play and share what you are passionate about, whatever that is The Destiny plan moves forward no matter what — Josh Deane (@S14deane) October 30, 2026

I may have worded this clumsily but this is the true heart of what I was trying to say Truly care about community healing and believe that it will help our studio bridge into the future in the most healthy way possible ❤️ Play and share what you are passionate about, whatever that is The Destiny plan moves forward no matter what

When one player suggested they feared they were being encouraged to purchase but never download Marathon just to support Bungie, Deane said , "Oh, don't buy Marathon as a donation or offer anything else."

"It's our job to show up for you," he added. When another fan expressed similar concern, he said , "I truly love the sentiment but only buy or play a thing that inspires you from us / you think is cool! We will find our way back home with Destiny."

So, there you have it: Destiny and Marathon don't depend upon the success of the other. As Bungie principal comms manager Dylan Gafner said , "Two cakes! One big community." That should offer some relief not only to Destiny players who feared their favorite game's future may still be in jeopardy but also to Marathon players who have feared the same.

Negativity has surrounded both games in recent months, with community members on each side going at each other as both struggled. For now, we know that the Destiny franchise will live on with a few projects. These include "celebration" content updates, a project that the team has teased as "Destiny 'Legacy'," and a mysterious "redacted" project.

For Marathon, Bungie will continue to try to revitalize the extraction shooter with Symbiosis this December. The studio also recently reassured players that the extraction component is "still a major part" of the experience as the team experiments with PvE and Deathmatch modes.

What's next for Destiny and Marathon remains to be seen, but it's clear Bungie is putting in the work to keep both afloat. While we wait to see how things pan out, you can see why the studio believes the latter struggled at launch . You can also read about how the Destiny community banded together to help the #SaveMassEffect movement .

articles.title: How To Upgrade Weapons, Medicines, and Trinkets - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero is action-packed with intense combat that can be both entertaining and unforgiving. Soul, the protagonist, can become a killing machine, but
articles.body:
Phantom Blade Zero is action-packed with intense combat that can be both entertaining and unforgiving. Soul, the protagonist, can become a killing machine, but miss a dodge or parry counter and he's done. You need to be prepared with the right tools and upgrades. That's why, in this guide, we will show you how to upgrade weapons, medicines, and trinkets in Phantom Blade Zero so that you always have the right tool and stat boost in your battles.

How To Upgrade Main Weapons and Phantom Edges

To upgrade your equipment in Phantom Blade Zero, you’re going to need Remnant Dust , which is your main currency, and materials such as Solvent and Forged Metal . All of these can be found scattered around areas while you explore every region.

First, you’ll need to meet Forge, the blacksmith located at the Outpost in Weeping Creek Valley . She will introduce herself as well as mention her two sisters, Jewel and Myst (we will go over them later in this guide).

Speak with her, and she will guide you with a tutorial on how to upgrade your equipment . After you complete the tutorial, your bell menu will expand , giving you the ability to upgrade equipment, along with having access to the store where you can purchase materials anytime you rest at a bell.

To upgrade, simply activate a bell, choose Upgrade Equipment , and select the weapon you want to upgrade. You can also revert and refund your materials if you decide to invest in a different weapon later.

The same goes for Phantom Edges , which are special weapons that consume Remnant Sparks and refill upon death. Similar to your standard weapons , after you upgrade a Phantom Edge to level 10, you’ll need a Phantom Reforge Talisman to revert it back to its initial level.

If you need an extra way to get materials, look no further than Quick Hand Zhang , a trinket collector whom you’ll find captured in Crimson Forest , just north of the Trail of Cages bell location.

Agree to save him, then progress through the cave to find a crank that will free him. From then on, you will have access to his store, also located in Crimson Forest, where you can purchase materials to upgrade your weapons even further.

Maximizing your health is key to surviving longer in Phantom Blade Zero, and there’s a variety of ways to do so, with items and upgrades that improve how you heal as well as how much you heal.

After the prologue, you begin your journey with a healing gourd that has 2 uses that refill upon death. Once you collect 5,000 Remnant Dust, you’ll want to activate Healing Art, which increases medicine uses by 1. You’ll find this upgrade by resting at a bell, selecting Train Abilities, then scrolling to the bottom branch to select and upgrade Healing Art and just like that! - your healing gourd increases from 2 to 3 uses.

As you progress in each area, you’ll find a variety of healing items that can be added alongside your initial gourd and even replace it if you like! These medicines you find will refill just like the Healing Gourd does– through dying and reviving or at a bell.

A good early game healing item to find is the Focus Pill, which you’ll discover in Weeping Creek Valley after defeating Peng Meng and acquiring his Dread Axe. You’ll use the axe to cut through the chains blocking the path, and then proceed up the dirt path to find the Axemaster’s Holding Cell bell.

From there, proceed through the wooden archway and then hang a left. You’ll again cut through chains with the axe, then head straight to the edge of the cliff where you will find the Focus Pill.

The Focus Pill reduces Sha-Chi consumption by 30%, and it gradually restores 30% HP over the same duration.

You can upgrade medicines as well . To do so, you’ll need to progress past the Village of Lu and into Pangzhen, where you’ll find the Green Serpent House . Here you can upgrade healing items with Remnant Dust and special items such as Apprentice Healer’s Memory , which can also be found by exploring the world.

Upgrading medicines can increase the percentage they heal and even increase their number of uses as well. You’ll also now be able to upgrade medicines from your bell menu anytime.

As for increasing the size of your health bar, you can do so by collecting Blue Memory Flowers . Each flower unlocks part of a memory, and once enough are collected to complete the memory, your maximum HP will increase by 5-10%, so it’s well worth the effort!

You can also have more health with other tools. You can equip accessories that focus on health boosts such as Jewel’s Knot , which increases your health bar even further, or the Medicine Case , which increases the percentage of healing you get by using a medicine.

To upgrade both trinkets and accessories, you’ll first need to find Jewel, Forge’s younger sister , located in the Village of Lu .

Jewel can polish and refine accessories and trinkets that you find in the world, upgrading them to help you further. For example, polishing the Battle Wraps will increase damage dealt to enemies from 5% to 10%.

Much like upgrading weapons with Forge and expanding your bell menu, you’ll now be able to upgrade accessories from any bell location after meeting Jewel.

As for fixing broken trinkets or story items such as the pipa, Jewel will explain that it is beyond her expertise and to take the missing pieces to Myst , the third and final sister located in Pangzhen . You’ll find Myst by using a crank that you’ll find in the wine cellar to open a secret door that will lead you down to her Tavern.

Not only will Myst restore the broken pipa, but she also specializes in Soul Tempering , where she extracts lingering memories from objects attuned to a weapon and infuses them into it. You’ll then be able to Soul Temper your main and Phantom Edge weapons when you have the right materials to do so, and your bell menu will also receive this option.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Prime Video in November
articles.body:
November is one of the most important times of the year for Amazon, thanks to Black Friday sales. So it's not surprising that Amazon's Prime Video would have an absolutely stacked slate of upcoming releases to entice new subscribers this month.

Along with the usual dump of movies getting added to the platform on November 1, we'll get quite a few highly anticipated Prime Video Originals. There's a Muhammand Ali series, Season 3 of Rings of Power, the Madden Movie, and a new Blade Runner series all premiering this month.

If you're wondering how to make the most of your Prime Video subscription this month, I've curated a quick selection of movies and shows that are absolutely worth your time. You can also jump to the full list of November releases to see the full breakdown by day.

Amazon, like every other streaming service, is dropping a bunch of Christmas movies onto its streaming service starting on November 1. Among this year's selection, there's one somewhat hidden gem worth highlighting: Jingle All the Way .

This is an Arnold Schwarzenegger film where he plays a mattress salesman who promises to get his son the year's hottest toy for Christmas, only to find out it's sold out everywhere. It's a ridiculous movie centered around consumerism that everyone needs to watch at least once.

The Greatest is a Prime Video Original biographical sports drama about the life of legendary boxer Muhammad Ali. This limited series runs for eight episodes (all of which drop at once), and will detail the early life, career, and rise of his boxing career. Jaelen Best plays the role of Cassius Clay/Muhammad Ali.

It's been a full two years since the last episode, but you can take a look at our review of Season 2 for a quick refresher on where we left off.

John Madden was a legend in the NFL community. He was a head coach, a broadcaster, and is quite literally the name associated with the popular Madden NFL video game series . Now that a few years have passed since his death, Nicolas Cage is taking a crack and portraying him in a drama biography. Cage is joined by a stacked cast, including Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, Matt Medrano, and Sienna Miller.

Madden will be available in theaters on November 11 before releasing on Prime Video a week later.

Taking place 50 years after the events of Blade Runner 2049 , this new series focuses on the power dynamic between replicants and humans shifting in the opposite direction. The show stars Hunter Schafer as a human pretending to be a replicant Blade Runner and Michelle Yeoh as an aging replicant Blade Runner in her final days. IGN had the chance to interview showrunner Silka Luisa, who called the series an "undercover police story" that's "quintessential Blade Runner."

All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will drop at once on Prime Video on November 25. There's also already a board game adaptation in the works for the series that will feature a different story.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Makes Surprise Cameo in New My Chemical Romance Animated Short
articles.summary: Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance.
articles.body:
Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance.

That's probably not the first sentence you expected to read heading into the Halloween weekend, but considering Kojima is known for his love of music, movies, games, and everything in between, it may not be too surprising. Still, fans of his work as a creative powerhouse were probably shocked to see him appear in the credits for the band's new animated short film, Prelude to The End .

The seven-and-a-half-minute project, which arrived as a surprise drop yesterday evening, is a stop-motion, dark fairytale based on director Lauren Tsai's The Dying World. Serving as a vehicle for a 20th anniversary music video for My Chemical Romance's "The End." – the opening track for the New Jersey group's seminal rock record, The Black Parade – the video also enlisted Kojima for a quick voice role.

Just as main character, Astrid, retreats to her room to parse through a few missed calls, we get Kojima's My Chemical Romance music video debut. He's credited simply as The Teacher, and can be heard scolding Astrid about late work in her third voicemail. You can see the full text below.

"Astrid your Japanese homework is late again. This is unacceptab-" Kojima's The Teacher can be heard saying before the recording is cut off.

Kojima is far from a stranger when it comes to cameos, but he's been especially busy in this department lately. The Metal Gear Solid series, which Kojima created and orchestrated for years, features a few moments where he broke the fourth wall for a cameo. He also appeared in CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077 for a role that he recently reprised in Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 .

HIDEO_KOJIMA (@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN) October 30, 2026

Kojima's collaboration with My Chemical Romance might have been especially exciting for the game creator, though, as his love for the band's music is well-documented. After posting about some of his favorite merch in early 2022, he shared that he attended one of the band's concerts in 2022. At the time, he said, "When I went to the venue, there were almost all teenage girls. I didn't see any old men in my age. But as I was wearing the band T-shirt, people said to me 'I like your T-shirt, Ojisan.'

Kojima also secretly teased his involvement in Prelude to The End when mentioning he had picked up the 20th Anniversary Edition of The Black Parade on vinyl just a few days ago. He then celebrated his involvement in the video with another post on X/Twitter.

Kojima is in good company when it comes to his My Chemical Romance cameo. Also featured in the list of Astrid's missed voicemails are Lost Weekend songwriter Phoebe Bridgers and Hit Me Hard and Soft hitmaker Billie Eilish. With both Grammy-Award-winning artists sharing a few seconds with Kojima, the moment definitely made sure to pack in as many heavy hitters as it could.

Kojima will seemingly continue to show up in side projects as he stays focused on other projects, including OD and Physint . Last night, we also got the first trailer for the anime spinoff series, Death Stranding Isolations . We know the Kojima Productions mastermind will appear in one live-action cameo , too, though what it will be has yet to be revealed.

articles.summary: After Defection, the next mission in our Call of Duty: Modern Warfare walkthrough is Counter Attack, another long and explosive chapter nearing the game's
articles.body:
After Defection , the next mission in our Call of Duty: Modern Warfare walkthrough is Counter Attack, another long and explosive chapter nearing the game's end. You once again take control of Park as allied forces try to take back enemy-occupied territory.

It’s lovely that the enemy is nice enough to keep Ghost’s mask on even when they’re tied up. Anyway, after the cutscene, you find yourself in a Normandy-like situation as the counter attack to retake Hajin City is underway. Using the other trucks as cover, move up only when Jae instructs unless you want to meet an early grave. Keep going until West pops smoke, allowing you and Jae to meet Dunn in a foxhole.

A friendly corporal bites the dust, so pick up his scope to call in air support

Equip the scope using D-pad Up , and aim for the locations enemies are pinning you down from. There are three buildings to target; one in the middle, one on the left, and finally the highrise to the right. Next, call in a strike on the BMP directly in front of you, as well as on a squad to its right.

Capture the Enemy Hardpoint With Your Squad

Move up after the line is cleared, using your own armored tank as cover and taking out infantry on foot. Head into the restaurant once friendlies enter, and go with Jae to go room to room to flush out any remaining enemies. This area has armored enemies, so make sure your clips are full before engaging.

Meet back up with Dunn and head up the stairs, taking out a couple enemies. Open the door at the top of the stairs, then head left into the apartment. Unfortunately, a family of civilians has fallen victim to the northern invaders. You can hear gunfire in the next apartment, so reach the wall in the bedroom to plant a breach charge by holding square. Blast through the wall and take out the enemies in front and on either side of you.

Exit the apartment and head up the stairs with Jae and Dunn, where you’ll find another door where you can hear enemy fire. Open the door for Jae and take out the two baddies on the rooftop.

Head outside and turn right, then jump down onto the scaffolding and descend back to the street level.

Continue following Jae as you meet up with a handful of other squads continuing the invasion. Follow behind one of the friendly armored trucks to interact with backpacks containing spare ammo and armor plates. Continue forward until heavy enemy artillery from the hotel starts raining down, where Jae directs the squad to take a left turn.

Keep following the squad into an open-air construction site. Enemy fire starts pelting the group, so pull out the scope to mark their locations for friendly artillery to wipe them out.

Destroy the MG Nests Defending the Construction Site

Request artillery on the machine gun nests in the half-built buildings directly ahead, being careful not to get shot. One nest is on the right and another on the left.

With the machine gun nests out of the way, clear out the remaining stragglers to secure the area. Use the armored trucks as cover, or climb them for a better view of enemies above you. On the left rear of the armored truck is FiNN LMG, so swap your pistol out for that to help support your assault. There are dozens of enemies remaining on both the bottom and top floors of the smaller construction area in the middle, so focus your fire on when their heads pop up or toss a grenade to proceed.

Follow Pvt. Morgan to breach the door to the apartment building, then climb the stairs with Jae. Head right, where a few SMG-equipped enemies meet you. Take them out, then help Jae lift some debris to clear the path forward

Crawl up the debris with Jae to find the hotel in plain view.

Call For Support on the Enemy Anti-Tank Unit

Using the scope, call for a friendly artillery strike on the enemy unit on a high floor in the hotel.

Wait for West to blast them, then support the rest of your allies as enemy infantry and a tank arrive, taking them out with the cars as cover. Continue forward slowly, using the friendly armored as cover once again. Make sure to stock up on ammo and armor plates if you need. After fighting down the street, you’ll meet up with a couple other friendly armored vehicles, but our goal is the hotel to your right.

Wait for the truck to drive through the wall, then assault your enemy with the rest of your squad. Secure the area by taking out all the enemies in the lobby. There are a few different guys to kill on either side of you, as well as above the lobby and on the stairs.

Head up the lobby stairs once it’s safe, and find the rest of the boys at the elevator. Dunn suggests the squad takes the elevator up to save time, much to the rest of everyone else’s dismay.

Locate the North Korean Forward Operating Site

Exit the elevator and head right with the team to a set of double doors that leads outside. Open the door and take out the enemies manning the position. Ascend the ruins of the hotel and meetup with the poor bastards who took the stairs, and clear out an apartment until you start to hear nearby gunfire.

Head back out the way you came and head left to other apartment, where Dunn and some of your other allies are pinned down. Join them, then take out the enemies hiding behind the flipped over table, and one hiding on the left in the living room. Careful when you cross into the next room, as there’s another enemy in the bedroom left of the living room that you can’t quite see from the entrance. Kill that one, then head to other bedroom to take out the enemy in the bathroom.

Go back out into the hallway with your squad to reach the conference room door. Join Jae at the door, and interact ( Square ) with him to start the breach. In classic Call of Duty fashion, breaching the door triggers a slow motion section that allows you to take out enemies without harming any of their civilian hostages.

Make your way back into the hallway and follow Dunn up the stairs. Pang warns you to stay quiet, and when you open the door to the outside comms relay, the enemies are none the wiser.

There’s a comms officer at the desk, so slowly sneak over and melee kill him. Or just go in guns blazing and take everyone else out, it doesn’t make a difference. There are a few guys to the right of where the comms officer was, as well as above you on the left.

After confirming to West that the comms relay is secured, he requests we provide overwatch support on allies below.

Head to the edge of the building and grab the KG-7 Vulcan sniper rifle, then pull out the scope again to get a good view of the street.

Eliminate Enemy Forces Defending the Parking Structure

Look to your right to see enemies spilling out on the roof of a parking structure above where friendlies are making their way down the street. Mark their location with the scope for artillery to take them out.

As enemies swarm from all over, focus your attention to the building on the left, where RPGs are poised to take out the allied convoy.

Once they’re out, three tanks arrive. Use the missile launchers next to you to blow them to smithereens. You’ll have to wait a bit for the launcher to get reloaded, so use that time to pick off any enemies with your sniper rifle.

With the way forward clear, friendly armor ma

kes their way up the street to take City Hall. A sniper starts raining down fire on the squad from the building on your left, so take him out ASAP. On the building to the right of where the sniper was is a mortar team just begging to get snipe, so kindly oblige them. Another tank spawns, so use the launcher one final time to save the day.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Designers Detail Reality Fracture’s Jace Arc, Echoed Pairs, and Secret Lair Bundles
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering designers Yoni Skolnik and Meris Mullaley break down Reality Fracture’s Jace storyline, Echoed Pairs pack changes, and the future of Secret Lair bundles.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering’s Reality Fracture set is a Universes Within set after two Universes Beyond sets in succession, but it’s also a little different in that it showcases iconic Magic characters, spells, and more that have been transformed by Jace Beleren.

The Planeswalker has transformed the universe into how he feels it should be, and that means new versions of well-known cards in a sort of “What If?” scenario.

IGN sat down with Yoni Skolnik, former Magic pro and Principal Game Designer, and Meris Mullaley, Worldbuilding Design Manager, to talk about the set’s influences, what comes in a pack, and the Secret Lair bundle.

Magic’s Designers Talk Reality Fracture Influences

Alternate universes are nothing new in pop culture, but I was curious how much last year’s Marvel’s Spider-Man set influenced Reality Fracture. As you can imagine, the genesis of Reality Fracture comes from a much earlier set.

“Some of the ideas go back to Planar Chaos, a set from 2007 that had a lot of What If elements,” Skolnik revealed.

“That set focused on messing with Magic's color pie, putting effects in colors where you wouldn't normally expect them.”

“While we didn't want to return to that exact formula for a What If set, the concept of What If is very compelling as it lets you pay tribute to Magic's devoted fan base.”

“Mark Rosewater [Head Designer] was keen to try the concept again, and it ended up fitting perfectly with the conclusion to Jace's storyline.”

“When developing the Echoed Pairs, most of our learnings came from other Magic IP sets that featured multiple legends,” Mullaley added.

“We chose characters who were (or could plausibly be) active in this current moment of Magic’s timeline. Creatively, we also kept most characters on their home planes rather than showing a multiversal cast of characters arriving on Hexhaven to stop Jace.”

“This helped the story of Reality Fracture keep a narrower focus on the key characters and reduced the amount of “why is this person here” questions.”

“We also see three separate Planeswalker cards for Jace, and we took a similar approach as we did with legends from Edge of Eternities or The Lord of the Rings: Tales from Middle-earth, where we see a character at multiple points along their narrative. Each Jace represents a different point in his journey, reflecting his accumulation of power and readiness to enact his final plan.”

So what about Jace? The blue-hued Planeswalker has been around since Lorwyn in 2007, but has been in the background of events in recent sets.

“In terms of game mechanics, Empower Jace was perfect for making our main character very present even if you only lightly interact with the set,” Skolnik explained.

“For new Magic players who want to go down deeper into the history of Jace, there are a few cards that are specifically stronger with Jace Planeswalker cards, to make the process of going to look back at old cards feel rewarding.”

“Flavorfully, I was very impressed with how the worldbuilding team navigated the character. For new players, we're drawing on timeless fantasy tropes like ‘Dark Wizard's Tower’ and ‘Former Ally Turned Foe’ to make the story approachable, while still having plenty of deeper lore references in the art, and a gripping conclusion to Jace's storyline in the web fiction.”

“It also helps that Jace is such a deeply blue character, which makes understanding his role go hand in hand with understanding blue's place in the color pie. One of the first things many people learn about Magic is that blue players are evil, so having an archetypally blue villain was a natural fit!”

You hear that, blue players? You’re the bad guys here. Still, sticking with multiple versions of cards, I asked about how the Echoed Pairs have been received. For newcomers, Echoed Pairs include normal and Echoverse versions of cards, for example Karn, Argent Defender, and Karn, Gilded Guardian.

“The technology of guaranteeing 1 card from an exciting subset per pack has been very well received since debuting in Dominaria with 1 legend per pack,” Skolnik reveals.

“Going up to 3 legends per pack in Reality Fracture was necessary to guarantee echoed pairs given our printers' constraints, and it made for very exciting packs that fans are loving.”

“I trust we'll one day find another place to deploy this technology of 3 cards in a pack that is linked somehow. This experimentation was not directly related to the 2027 pack changes, but together they show the breadth of problems our production teams face while balancing Magic design's need for constant novelty and reinvention against the reality of what it takes to print all the Magic product for our growing audience!”

In the time since we spoke with the Wizards of the Coast team, the Reality Fracture Secret Lair Bundle has been delayed. We asked about whether it’ll be sticking around.

“Yes! Secret Lair Bundle will become a staple of Magic Multiverse sets and is expected to appear in those sets going forward.”

“Part of the impetus for launching these bundles was to consolidate Special Bundles into one incredible package that we could repeat set over set. The theming of Reality Fracture and how we explore Jace’s inner sanctum made a lot of thematic sense to use as the jumping-off point for this new product line.”

So, onto the big question then: as someone who can’t believe their luck by packing Craterclaw Colossus and Hexhaven Invigorator, I was curious what the team’s favorite cards from Reality Fracture were.

“ I really love both Ajani Planeswalker cards,” Skolnik explained.

“Seeing Ajani Resolute in standard Life Gain decks has been great. A 2-mana Planeswalker is very tricky to balance, but with Planeswalkers such a big part of the set, I really wanted to try and print one here.”

“Ajani Unrelenting has been demolishing in draft, but I’m also excited to see it doing work in Commander decks built around Planeswalkers.”

Mullaley’s pick was spoiler-filled, so look away, lore fans.

“Vindictive Triumph depicts one of my favorite moments in the fiction, where [spoilers] Liliana resurrects her Echoverse doppelgänger as a lich and takes the fight to Jace. I read that moment in an early draft of the story and knew immediately it needed to be a card.”

For more on Magic: The Gathering’s current set, check out Reality Fracture’s most expensive cards , as well as the most powerful precons of all time .

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .
